entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Edmund Veesenmayer was a high-ranking German SS functionary and Holocaust perpetrator during the Nazi era. He significantly contributed to the Holocaust in Hungary and in the Independent State of Croatia (NDH). Veesenmayer was a subordinate of Ernst Kaltenbrunner and Joachim von Ribbentrop, and worked with Adolf Eichmann. He was involved in dismembering Czechoslovakia in 1939,
in the establishment of the Ustaše-run NDH puppet state following the April 1941 German invasion of Yugoslavia, and in the selection and installation of the 1941–1944 puppet regime of Milan Nedić in the German-occupied territory of Serbia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Edmund Veesenmayer played a significant role in the Holocaust in Hungary and Croatia, contributing to the dismemberment of Czechoslovakia and the establishment of puppet regimes. His actions had regional consequences, affecting the lives of thousands during World War II.
